newsitem.title: USA: US late spot prods jump smartly on futures rally.
newsitem.headline: US late spot prods jump smartly on futures rally.

text.p: U.S. spot products prices jumped sharply by late Monday afternoon amid a NYMEX rally and a late-afternoon firming on differentials for Gulf Coast conventional unleaded gasoline, players said.

Heating oil prices jumped about 2.35 cents a gallon in New York Harbor tracking NYMEX, with differentials holding steady at about 0.50 cent over February futures. Prompt back-1st-cycle Gulf heat diffs were talked about 0.25 cent firmer at 3.80 cents below February futures, although few deals were spotted.
NYMEX values were helped by 10-day forecasts calling for normal to below-normal temperatures in the Northeast, the world's largest heating oil market, traders said.

On the gasoline front, Gulf Coast conventional unleaded "M4" grade saw diffs firm 0.75 cent to 2.25 cents below the print, players said. "A lot of people are expecting refinery turnarounds and some export gasoline volumes are going to South America and the Caribbean," one trader said, citing bullish factors.
Traders said skimpy U.S. gasoline inventories -- hovering near their lowest point in over 25 years -- were also lending price support.

Differentials on New York Harbor conventional unleaded were little changed at 1.55 cents below the screen despite the low stocks and reports Tosco Corp had taken down a 140,000 barrel per day fluid catalytic cracking unit at its Bayway refinery in New Jersey for several weeks of maintenance.
